newsitem.title: USA: Dow Jones index sets 30th record high for year.
newsitem.headline: Dow Jones index sets 30th record high for year.

text.p: The Dow Jones industrial average set its 30th record high for the year Thursday as earnings reports streamed in with hardly a nasty surprise and bonds were bolstered by fresh signs of a moderately growing economy.
The Dow closed up 38.39 points at 6,059.20, surpassing Wednesday's record close of 6,020.81. It was also the index's third high for the week.
In the broader market, advancing issues led declines 1,406 to 944 on heavy volume of 478 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.

"We're seeing for the most part a continuation of a favourable interpretation of earnings news coming out and today's economic reports support the thesis the economy is growing at a rate even Goldilocks cannot quibble with -- not too hot or too cold," said Jim Solloway, director of research at Argus Research.
Other market gauges also set new highs. The Standard & Poor's composite index of 500 stocks rose 2.58 to 706.99 -- its third record close for the week.
The NYSE Composite was up 1.88 to a record 376.41, topping its previous high of 374.74 set Oct. 7.
The technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index, however, fell for a second day, losing 9.03 points at 1,241.96, despite more good earnings news.
Struggling computer maker Apple Computer late Wednesday stunned investors by reporting an unexpected $25 million fourth quarter profit after posting heavy losses earlier in the year.
Apple rose 5/8 to 26-3/8, Intel lost 1-7/8 to 110-3/4 and Oracle was off 3/4 to 43-3/4. Microsoft fell 2-1/2 to 135-1/2.
The market also was buoyed by the latest data that showed a slowing economy, which was expected to lessen the odds that the Federal Reserve will raise interest rates any time soon.
Construction starts on new homes and apartments in September posted their biggest drop in 21 months, falling 6 percent to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 1.438 million.
Building permits, a precursor of housing starts, were down 2.9 percent, indicating that starts would remain soft over the next two or three months.
Also, production by the nation's mines, factories and utilities grew more slowly in September, partly because of a continued slowdown in the auto industry.
In the Treasury market, the 30-year Treasury bond was up three-quarters of a point, lowering its yield to 6.80 percent from 6.86 percent late Wednesday.
Ironically the stock market's gains come as the ninth anniversary of Black Monday looms. On Oct. 19, 1987, the Dow plummeted 508.00 points or 22.61 percent.
Analysts said the big difference between now and 1987 was that interest rates were then at 10 percent and rising, while they are currently steadying and are less than 7 percent.
"I was scared in October 1987 and a bit concerned in October 1989 but these were Octobers where the market was out of sync with fundamentals," said Solloway.
Among individual stocks, PepsiCo rose 5/8 to 29-3/4 on rumours that it could be a takeover target of Philip Morris, whose stock gained 1-1/4 to 97-3/8. Company officials declined comment.

General Instrument lost 4-1/2 to 22-3/8 after reporting third-quarter earnings that fell short of expectations. The company also warned that its fourth-quarter and 1997 earnings will be disappointing.
Micron rose 1 to 32-1/8 after Merrill Lynch said Micron is poised to report a substantial upside surprise in its earnings for the quarter ending in November.
Merck, which Wednesday reported unexpectedly strong quarterly results, surged 3 to 75.
Among initial public offerings, XLConnect Solutions, a unit of microcomputer maker Intelligent Electronics, skyrocketed 12-7/8 points or 86 percent to 27-7/8 in its first day of trading.
Metro Networks, a provider of traffic reports, local news, sports and weather to television and radio broadcasters, surged to 20-1/2 from its $16 a share pricing.
The American Stock Exchange index was up 0.87 to 577.39.
The average NYSE share was up 20 cents.
The Wilshire Associates Equity Index -- the market value of NYSE, American and Nasdaq issues -- was at a record high of 6,915.533 up 19.505 or 0.28 percent.
